s: A medium-sized publishing house founded in 1927, Coward-McCann was joined with the firm G.P. Putnam’s in 1936 to publish titles such as playwright Thornton Wilder’s Our Town. In 1959, John Geoghegan joined Coward-McCann as editor-in-chief. Two years later, he was named president, then chairman.

t: BOOK PUBLISHER QUITS, ATTACKS NEW 'MENTALITY' - The New York Times
s: June 18, 1981 - Israel, himself the author of four books, said: ''I don't feel that we've treated Coward, McCann anything like a stepchild. I am genuinely shocked by what Jack said, and I feel great regret that if he feels that way he never talked to me about it. Whether his opinion about the company or mine is right, only time will tell.'' Mr. Geoghegan said: ''The fact is that when the instruments of publishing authority are removed from the house - a strong voice in advertising, promotion, sales goals and the effective way to sell subsidiary rights - and turned over to corporate decision makers, publishing becomes a parent-house operation,'' he said.
